topic: Which country has the most elephants? (Botswana — ~131,900 savanna elephants, KAZA survey 2022)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Kenya or South Africa has the most elephants.
myths.reality: Botswana holds ~130,000 — the top national population; Zimbabwe is second (~65,000); Kenya ~36,000; South Africa ~30,000 (KAZA 2022; national censuses).

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

screen_exempt: ^A was right|^B was right|^C was right

landscape.our_gap: Feed answers say 'Botswana' with a stock elephant; nobody shows the northern range on the map with the KAZA count, the 1-in-3 share and the IUCN status.

kaza_2022.title: KAZA Elephant Survey 2022 — results
kaza_2022.notes: aerial survey Aug–Oct 2022: 227,900 elephants across KAZA; Botswana 131,909 (top national population); Zimbabwe 65,028

iucn_savanna.title: Loxodonta africana — African Savanna Elephant
iucn_savanna.notes: assessed 2020, published 2021: Endangered; population decline of at least 60% over three generations (~50 years)

unesco_okavango.title: Okavango Delta
unesco_okavango.notes: inscribed 2014; permanent marshland and seasonally flooded plains in the Kalahari; home to the world's largest population of elephants

wiki_botswana_elephants.title: Elephants in Botswana
wiki_botswana_elephants.notes: ≈130,000 elephants, about a third of Africa's total; concentrated in the north (Chobe, Okavango); KAZA 2022 count 131,909

britannica_chobe.title: Chobe National Park
britannica_chobe.notes: northern Botswana; known for one of the largest concentrations of elephants in Africa

natgeo_elephants.title: Botswana has more elephants than any other country
natgeo_elephants.notes: ~130,000 elephants, a third of Africa's remaining savanna elephants; Chobe and the Okavango

gec_2016.publisher: PeerJ — Great Elephant Census (Chase et al. 2016)
gec_2016.title: Continent-wide survey reveals massive decline in African savannah elephants
gec_2016.notes: 352,271 savanna elephants in 18 surveyed countries (2014–15); Botswana ~130,000 = the largest share (~37%)

claims.text: Botswana has the top national elephant population: 131,909 counted in the 2022 KAZA aerial survey (~130,000).
vo: which country has the most elephants
botswana: about one hundred and thirty thousand savanna elephants, more than any other country

claims.text: That is roughly a third of Africa's savanna elephants (352,271 counted in the 2014–15 Great Elephant Census), in a country of about 2.5 million people.
vo: roughly a third of all africa's elephants, in a country of two and a half million people

claims.text: Botswana's elephants are concentrated in the north — Chobe National Park and the Okavango Delta (UNESCO 2014), an inland wetland on the edge of the Kalahari.
vo: most of them roam the north: chobe national park and the okavango delta, a wetland in the desert

claims.text: The African savanna elephant is listed Endangered by the IUCN (2021), with a decline of at least 60 % over ~50 years.
vo: across africa the savanna elephant is listed as endangered, down more than half in fifty years

claims.text: One country holds about a third of the continent's herd.
